leaders.headline: Developers increasingly direct, review and validate.

quotes.quote: …programming via LLM agents is increasingly becoming a default workflow for professionals, except with more oversight and scrutiny.
quotes.speaker: Andrej Karpathy

quotes.quote: Our engineers are orchestrating fully autonomous digital task forces, firing off agents and accomplishing incredible things.
quotes.speaker: Sundar Pichai

quotes.quote: These developers moved from writing code to architecting and verifying the implementation work that is carried out by AI agents.
quotes.speaker: Thomas Dohmke
quotes.role: then CEO of GitHub, with Eirini Kalliamvakou

leaders.balance: 48% trust AI when they can easily verify its answers — only 7% trust it with important decisions.

shiftAction.headline: Never delegate what you can't verify.
actions: Give an agent one real task
Bounded, in a real repository — not a toy demo.
Run it. Try to break it. Ask why each change is there.
The negative case: the token that should fail.
That list is your learning plan.
shiftAction.evidence: 66% of developers say their biggest frustration is AI output that is “almost right, but not quite.”
shiftAction.action: This week: one real task, one agent — and proof before you ship.

studentPlan.headline: Learn with AI. Prove it without AI.

columns.label: Skills
items: Programming, data structures & algorithms
HTTP, APIs & SQL
Git & testing
Auth & OWASP basics
Reading code you didn't write

columns.label: Habits
items: First version by hand — AI explains, doesn't solve
Then ask AI for an alternative; explain the trade-off
A 30-minute AI-off kata
Log what the AI got wrong
Teach back one concept

columns.label: Project
items: One small API, built twice
v1 by hand · v2 extended with an agent
README, AGENTS.md and a process log
Negative tests · “3 AI mistakes I caught”
A 5-minute walkthrough video

tools: ChatGPT study mode · Claude learning mode · Gemini Guided Learning · CS50.ai
GitHub Copilot (free for verified students) · Cursor
Claude Code · OpenAI Codex · Gemini CLI
studentPlan.evidence: Andrew Ng on “don't learn to code”: “This advice will be seen as some of the worst career advice ever given.” · Lee et al. (CHI 2025): the more people trust AI, the less critical thinking they report.
studentPlan.action: This month: build one small API by hand, extend it with an agent — and explain both.

educatorRollout.headline: Change one assignment this term.

columns.label: This month
items: An AI rule for every assignment: secure lane (AI-off, oral) or open lane (AI scaffolded)
— or the five-level AI Assessment Scale
Every lecturer runs an agent on their own assignment

columns.label: This term
items: One assignment per course adds a 5‑minute oral defence
A planted-bug review and a live change request
A process log
One rubric, calibrated across staff

columns.label: This year
items: AI-off checkpoints and an agentic capstone
A monthly staff community of practice
Compare grades with oral-defence results
Update the syllabus: keep, shift, add, prove

educatorRollout.evidence: 95% of UK undergraduates use AI — only 48% feel their teaching staff help them build AI skills (HEPI 2026). Purdue rebuilt 22 courses and 300+ plans of study for its AI‑competency requirement.
educatorRollout.action: This term: change one assignment — AI allowed, explanation required.

first90.headline: Your first 90 days.

columns.label: Stand out
items: A project with a process log
One merged open-source PR
An “AI mistakes I caught” write-up
Explain every line

columns.label: Days 1–30
items: Set up the agent with the team's context files
Read the codebase with AI as a guide
Fix three small bugs — first attempt by hand

columns.label: Days 31–60
items: Issue → plan → agent → verify → PR
A negative test with every change
Pair with a senior on one agent session

columns.label: Days 61–90
items: One small feature, end to end
A written design rationale
Catch one bug before review

first90.evidence: Daily AI users reached their 10th pull request in 49 days, vs 91 days without AI (DX, six enterprises).
first90.action: Make it visible: every PR explained, every agent mistake logged.

roadmap.headline: Adopt, train and measure — together.

columns.label: Days 1–30
items: A clear AI stance and guardrails: data, security, review rules
Two or three workflows, with pilot teams
Baseline delivery and quality before rollout
Context files in key repositories

columns.label: Days 31–60
items: Training by career stage — not one workshop
Mentoring through agent-session reviews
Update onboarding and one competency row

columns.label: Days 61–90
items: Compare with the baseline: delivery, quality, capability — not seats
Scale or stop each workflow
Update development plans and promotion criteria

roadmap.evidence: DORA's AI Capabilities Model: clear AI stance · healthy data ecosystems · AI-accessible internal data · strong version control · small batches · user-centric focus · quality internal platforms. BCG: regular use is sharply higher with at least five hours of training.
roadmap.action: Start Monday: baseline first — then adopt, train and measure together.
